name: The Christmas Train at Kirby Family Farm
when_note: Gates open 6 PM, first train 6:30 PM, last ride about 9 PM, gates close 10 PM
cost: $19.99 ages 10 and up and $12.99 ages 3 to 9 in advance ($25 and $15 at the gate if available), free for ages 2 and under
paras: Kirby Family Farm in Williston runs its 15th annual Christmas Train on select nights from November 27 through December 26, 2026. Guests ride a narrow gauge locomotive on a 20 minute trip through thousands of Christmas lights around the farm, and the farm says many nights sell out.

The ticket also covers a visit with Santa, a magic show on the depot stage, a Christmas buddies meet and greet and dance party, a tractor ride to a lost Christmas town, an Italian carousel, an antique Ferris wheel and an elf gift surprise for children 10 and under. Photos with Santa and the mascots are free with your own camera or phone.
The nonprofit farm works with at risk and special needs children, and ticket money supports its programs. After Christmas, the December 26 night leaves out the Santa visit.
tip: Pre-register for your night, since many dates sell out and advance ticket holders may get early entry.

name: Christmas in the Quarry at Cedar Lakes Woods and Gardens
when_note: 5:30 to 8 PM, arrive before 3 PM for full daylight garden access
cost: Adults $10, ages 6 to 13 $5, ages 5 and under free
paras: Cedar Lakes Woods and Gardens, a 20 acre nonprofit botanical garden inside a restored limestone quarry in Williston, holds Christmas in the Quarry on December 12, 13, 17, 19, 20, 22 and 23, 2026. Hours are 5:30 to 8 PM, and guests who arrive before 3 PM also get full daylight access to the gardens.

The annual walkthrough light show has twinkling lighted pathways, glowing quarry walls and illuminated waterfalls, plus live holiday entertainment, food and drink vendors, holiday shopping from local artisans and photos with Santa Claus. Each ticket is good for one admission on any one event day, and tickets are nonrefundable.

The standard trail is about one mile with elevation changes, and the garden says families with strollers or wheelchairs should stay on the fairly level top trail. Only service animals are allowed during the special events, and parking is included with admission.
tip: Take the level top trail if you are pushing a stroller, since the full trail has steeper sections.

name: Holiday at Santa Fe College
venue: Santa Fe College Sasser Fine Arts Hall
paras: Santa Fe College Fine Arts presents Holiday at Santa Fe on Saturday, December 5, 2026, with shows at 2 PM and 6 PM in the Jackson N. Sasser Fine Arts Hall. Ticket prices run from free to $20 on the college's ticket page.

Santa Fe College Performing Arts, the SF Teaching Zoo, the SF Planetarium and the SF Little School team up on an interactive performance. Perry the mouse and Santa Claus journey through a forest to make it snow inside the hall, with familiar holiday music, and a meet and greet with animals follows in the lobby.
The show is directed by Assistant Professor of Dance Melissa Brenner and is funded in part by Visit Gainesville, Alachua County.
tip: Stay after the show for the animal meet and greet in the lobby.
